subject: Re: Dedicated migration — temporary capacity safety net & credit amortization
messages:
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated migration — sizing and credits Qs

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Atlas is close to deciding on moving a subset of our prod traffic from your hosted API to a dedicated GPU pool. Before we finalize, procurement asked for a clear proposal that explains:

- How conversion credits would be applied to our committed monthly spend (we expect a 12-month commitment).
- Whether you offer a short-term capacity safety net (we have a big internal spike expected in Jan) — specifically: bridge months with guaranteed throughput or temporary burst capacity.
- How credits amortize if we scale the pool up/down in the first 90 days.

Attached is a snapshot of our current monthly token usage and expected spike (atlas_demand_snapshot_q3.csv). Can you put something formal together by COB next Tuesday? Procurement wants numbers to run through their finance model.

Appreciate it — Evan

--
Evan Ross
VP Engineering, Atlas Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated migration — sizing and credits Qs

Evan —

Thanks for the data. I pulled the file and ran a quick pass with Marcus on sizing. High-level proposal below; we'll put a PDF together with line items and an MLP-style amortization schedule.

1) Conversion credits and amortization
- Offer: 3 months of gross hosted spend converted to dedicated credits, applied as a monthly credit against committed invoice for months 1-6 (front-loaded but spread partly into months 4-6 to smooth GAAP impact).
- If you scale up within the first 90 days, unused credits roll forward and re-amortize over remaining credit months (no cash refunds). If you scale down, credits cover the committed minimum; any over-commitment is handled per the True-Up clause.

2) Temporary capacity safety net (bridge months)
- We can provide 2 burst months (+25% throughput) available in months 1-4 as part of the onboarding package. Bursts are gated by a short activation window (48h notice) and subject to a per-burst usage price at a discounted rate.
- Optionally, we can add a guaranteed throughput floor for month 1 to ensure no cold-start throttling while KV caches warm.

3) Throughput guarantees and SLA buckets
- Base SLO: 99.5% request success latency under target seq-length profile for provisioned pool.
- For Jan spike we can commit to an elevated SLO for the burst months for requests routed to the dedicated pool; fallback policy to hosted if sustained beyond burst allowances.

Next steps: Marcus will draft the pricing PDF and amortization table. Karthik, can you confirm the accounting-friendly wording and whether we should offer an alternate 6-month amortization (so credits are less front-loaded)?

Evan — we'll aim to get the formal proposal in your inbox by Tue COB (Nov 24).

Best,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated migration — sizing and credits Qs

Mina / Marcus —

I reviewed the proposed amortization approach. Two quick notes for sales/legal/finance:
- Alternate 6-month amortization is fine, but offer the 3-month front-loaded version as the standard with the 6-month as a concession for larger deals (> $250k/mo committed).
- For burst months, make the activation fees explicit: a fixed activation fee + per-token discounted overage. That avoids open-ended exposure.

I'm attaching a short clause draft you can paste into the proposal PDF. Also recommend a short mutual-action-plan doc that lists dates for onboarding, KV-cache warm-up validation, and a Jan spike readiness check.

Karthik
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed dedicated pricing and safety-net options (attached)

Evan / Lisa —

Attached is a formalized proposal: proposed-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf and a short mutual-action-plan (mutual-action-plan-ATLAS.docx). Summary of the key commercial points:

- Committed capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (pool sizing based on your Q3 snapshot + 25% buffer).
- Monthly commit: $210,000/mo.
- Conversion credits: equal to 3 months of current hosted invoice; applied as credits across months 1-6 (3-month front-load default). Alternate 6-month smoothing available.
- Bridge months: two burst months (+25% throughput) at 40% discount to on-demand overage price; activation fee $3,000 per burst.
- SLA: 99.5% availability and latency SLOs for provisioned pool; financial credits capped per month (standard SLA language).

Notes: We modeled Jan spike and confirmed the 25% burst should cover your forecasted peak if activated early (48 hours). If spike extends beyond the two bursts, traffic will be routed back to hosted at on-demand rates unless we execute a temporary scale-up (quote provided separately).

Next steps: If this looks good, I'll share a DocuSign link for the term sheet and the MLP. We can also schedule a 30-min convo with Atlas finance for the amortization modelling.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf, mutual-action-plan-ATLAS.docx
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed dedicated pricing and safety-net options (attached)

Marcus / Mina / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. Procurement reviewed and likes the 6-month smoothing for credits (easier for our internal amortization). Two quick asks before we send to our CFO:

1) Can you move one of the burst months to be pre-scheduled for Jan 1 to Jan 31 (so we don't need to rely on 48h activation for that primary expected spike)? The second burst can be on-demand.
2) Please include a one-paragraph clause confirming that credits will re-amortize if we add GPUs in the first 90 days (you outlined this already, but procurement wants explicit language in the term sheet).

If you can update the term sheet with those two changes we'll route it to legal. Otherwise this looks close to final.

Evan

--
Evan Ross
VP Engineering, Atlas Health
